t: You're on King Charles Street in Westminster, a street that links Whitehall in the east with Horse Guards Road in the west. Large government offices flank it to the north and south. The street is named for Charles II, who was King of Scotland from 1649 until 1651, and King of England, Scotland and Ireland from the Restoration of the monarchy in 1660 until his death in 1685. So you're walking through the heart of government on a street named for a restored king.
